functions.name: indicator_for
functions.signature: pub fn indicator_for(hook_status: &str, pb_state: &str, pb_progress: Option<u8>, hook_on: bool, osc_on: bool) -> Indicator
functions.behavior: Semantic half of Python progress_indicator (sidebar.py:695). Decides WHICH indicator a row carries, with no reference to the animation frame (frame resolution is deferred to the client's Indicator::resolve). Precedence: (1) if osc_on AND pb_state is an active state (not in INACTIVE_STATES = {"", "hidden"}): if pb_state == "indeterminate" return Progress{pct: None, state: Plain} (Plain => spinner inherits the row's own color, matching Python's `return spinner_frame(frame), None`); otherwise map pb_state via STATE_COLOR ({normal->Normal, paused->Paused, error->Error}) and ANY OTHER active state name -> Plain, then return Progress{pct: pb_progress, state}. (2) else if hook_on AND hook_status is "working" -> Progress{pct: None, state: Plain}; hook_status "attention" -> Attention. (3) else Indicator::None. This is where OSC wins over the hook glyph.
edge_cases: pb_progress = Some(0): must render as "0%" (Python: `0 is not None` is true, isdigit("0") true). Do NOT treat 0 as "no progress".

OSC active + non-indeterminate + pct None: Python returns a spinner COLORED by the state (color = STATE_COLOR.get(state)), NOT an uncolored spinner. Preserve by keeping state = Normal/Paused/Error (not Plain) so ProgressState::color() yields a color. This is the subtlest parity trap: a state=Normal pct=None spinner is GREEN, whereas an OSC-indeterminate spinner is row-colored (Plain).

Unknown active OSC state (not in {normal,paused,error,indeterminate,hidden,""}): Python STATE_COLOR.get() -> None, so it renders text (pct% or spinner) in the row's own color. Map unknown active states to state=Plain, pct passed through.

INACTIVE_STATES membership is exactly {"", "hidden"}: empty string (tmux too old to know pane_pb_state) and "hidden" (tmux 3.7 name for cleared/no progress) both mean no OSC indicator. Do not add others.
osc_on false: OSC branch skipped entirely even if pb_state is active — falls through to the hook glyph.
hook_status is any value other than "working"/"attention" (e.g. ""): yields Indicator::None once the OSC branch is skipped.
Both osc_on and hook_on false: always Indicator::None.

functions.name: Indicator::resolve
functions.signature: pub fn resolve(self, frame: usize) -> (String, Option<StateColor>)
functions.behavior: Client/painting half of Python progress_indicator: turns a semantic Indicator into the (text, color-key) actually drawn for animation frame `frame`. None -> ("", None). Attention -> ("●", None). Progress{pct: None, state} -> (spinner_frame(frame), state.color()). Progress{pct: Some(p), state} -> (format!("{p}%"), state.color()). Mirrors prototype main.rs:142.
edge_cases: Attention glyph is the literal U+25CF ● and never animates (static across frames).
Percentage text has no leading pad/sign; "100%" is 4 chars, "0%" is 2 — width feeds the right-edge reserve calc in the painter.
state.color() is None only for ProgressState::Plain; Normal/Paused/Error return the green/yellow/red state-color key. This is what makes an OSC percentage stand out from the row's own color.

functions.name: spinner_frame
functions.behavior: Returns SPINNER[frame % SPINNER.len()]. SPINNER is the 10 braille glyphs "⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏" (sidebar.py:686, prototype main.rs:34). Client painting concern; the frame counter advances on the wall clock every ANIM_INTERVAL=0.0625s (~16fps) independent of the data poll.
edge_cases: frame wraps via modulo; any usize is valid.
Each glyph is a single display column (braille) so the pinned right-edge indicator stays 1 column wide across all frames — do not substitute variable-width glyphs.

The set of spinner glyphs doubles as the "is this row animating?" test in the main loop (Python: `indicator in _SPINNER_FRAMES`). In the Rust split this must instead be Indicator::indeterminate() on the semantic rows, NOT a string membership test — see parity_risks.

functions.name: append_agent_rows
functions.signature: fn append_agent_rows(rows: &mut Vec<Row>, group: &[&AgentSession], window: &Window, pane_progress: &PaneProgressMap, hook_on: bool, osc_on: bool)
functions.behavior: Ports _append_agent_rows (sidebar.py:714). Appends one tree row per session in `group` under an already-emitted window heading. For index i (last = len-1): branch = "└─" if i==last else "├─". text = format!("   {branch} {label}") — NOTE the space between branch and label (agent rows differ from pane rows, which have no space). Looks up (pb_state, pb_progress) = pane_progress.get(session.pane) defaulting to ("", None), computes the indicator via indicator_for(session.status, pb_state, pb_progress, hook_on, osc_on). Row carries: kind Agent{ color: session.color (name string, may be empty), emphatic: status in {attention, working} }, key = RowKey::Agent(session.id, session.pane), the window it is filed under (so the client's activate() can focus the pane displaying the session), the pane id, and the indicator. In the Python the indicator (text+color) is baked onto the item; in the daemon/client split store the semantic Indicator and resolve at paint.
edge_cases: group is never empty when called (build_rows guards with `if group.is_empty() continue`), but a single-element group => that element gets "└─".
session.pane missing from pane_progress => default ("", None) => inactive OSC, so the hook glyph (if any) shows. Must replicate the .get(pane, ("",None)) default, not panic.
emphatic (bold) is driven by hook status (attention/working), NOT by the OSC indicator; a pane that only reports OSC progress but whose session has empty status is not bold. Keep these independent.

session.color empty string "" must fall back to the default agent color at paint time (Python `_agent_color_pairs.get(color or "")` then pair 2); carry the empty name through semantically, resolve in the color module.

The agent-row key includes the pane BECAUSE one session can be placed under several windows at once (recorded-if-occupied ∪ title-matched); the pane component is what keeps keys unique so nav/activate stay well-defined.

functions.name: build_rows
functions.signature: pub fn build_rows(windows: &[Window], sessions: &[AgentSession], pane_progress: &PaneProgressMap, pane_status: &PaneStatusMap, hook_on: bool, osc_on: bool) -> Vec<Row>
functions.behavior: Ports build_rows (sidebar.py:736). Produces the flat semantic row list. Structure: (1) header Row text " WINDOWS" (leading space), then a blank Row. (2) For each window in `windows` order: a Window row text format!("{marker} {index}: {name}") with marker '*' if active else ' ', kind Window{active, color(name)}, key RowKey::Window(window.id), no indicator. Then its panes: last = len-1; branch "└─"/"├─"; active '*' /' '; text format!("   {branch}{active}{index}: {title}") — NO space after branch, single-char active marker glued to index; kind Pane{color(name)}, key RowKey::Pane(pane.id), indicator = indicator_for(pane_status.get(pane.id).unwrap_or(""), pane.pb_state, pane.pb_progress, hook_on, osc_on). (3) For each distinct agent name in SORTED order over {s.agent for s in sessions}: push blank, header Row text format!(" {}", agent.to_uppercase()), blank. Then for each window in `windows` order, collect group = sessions with that agent whose window is this window; skip empty groups; emit a Window heading row with key RowKey::AgentWindow(agent, window.id) (DISTINCT from the top-section Window key for the same window) and text same as a normal window row; then append_agent_rows(group).
edge_cases: A window with zero panes still emits its Window heading row and no pane children (Python appends nothing; last = -1 never reached).
Windows with no matching agent sessions are skipped inside each agent section (group empty) but always appear in the top WINDOWS section.
Agent section ordering is `sorted(set(agent names))` — dedup then sort by Unicode scalar order. For ASCII names (claude, copilot) Rust str Ord matches Python. Sort AFTER dedup.
Header text has a single leading space (" WINDOWS", " CLAUDE"); do not trim it — it aligns the underline/bold heading.

agent.to_uppercase(): Python str.upper(); for ASCII agent names identical. Non-ASCII agent names could diverge (Python full-casing vs Rust to_uppercase) — agent names are lowercased identifiers so unlikely, but note it.

Window identity: Python files a session under a window via `s['window'] is w` (object identity, the same dict from fetch_windows). Rust must compare by window id equality; equivalent only because window ids are unique per server. Group membership order follows the `sessions` slice order within that window.

The same physical window appears TWICE with two different keys when it hosts agents: once as RowKey::Window in the WINDOWS section and once as RowKey::AgentWindow(agent,id) in the agent section. Selection/nav treat them as separate selectable rows — this is intentional and must be preserved.

Empty `sessions` => only the WINDOWS section (header, blank, windows/panes). Empty `windows` => header " WINDOWS", a blank, then any agent sections will emit their header+blanks but no window groups (every group empty) — matching Python.

functions.name: fit
functions.signature: pub fn fit(text: &str, field: usize) -> String
functions.behavior: Ports _fit (sidebar.py:808) / prototype fit (main.rs:498). CLIENT/painting concern. Fits text to exactly `field` COLUMNS counting by chars (code points, NOT display width): field==0 -> "". char_count > field -> if field==1 return "…" (U+2026) else take first field-1 chars + "…". else left-justify: text + spaces to reach `field` chars. The right-pad is what keeps the reverse-video selection bar solid across the whole row.
edge_cases: field == 0 returns empty string (Python `if field <= 0`; usize can't be negative, so `== 0`).
Overflow with field == 1 returns a lone "…" (never text[:0]+…).
Ellipsis is exactly one char U+2026; ensure the truncated slice length is field-1 chars so total == field chars.
Counts CHARS not grapheme/display width: a wide CJK title is counted as its char count, matching Python len(); do not switch to unicode-width here or parity with the reserve math breaks.
When text already == field, returns it unchanged (no ellipsis, no pad).
Padding must be spaces to reach `field` CHARS (Python ljust); count added spaces from char count, not byte length.

parity_risks: Daemon(semantic-rows) vs client(painting) split: Python bakes the resolved indicator STRING (spinner glyph for the current frame) plus the resolved curses color pair onto each row inside build_rows/_append_agent_rows, then rebuilds every animation frame. The Rust daemon must instead emit rows carrying a SEMANTIC Indicator enum (None/Attention/Progress{pct,state}) and color NAME strings; the client resolves spinner_frame(frame), _fit, and the terminal Color at paint time. Getting this boundary wrong (baking glyphs in the daemon) forces a full row rebuild + re-serialize every 62ms.

Spinner-color subtlety: an OSC active state that is NOT indeterminate and has pb_progress==None must yield a spinner COLORED by the state (green/yellow/red), while OSC 'indeterminate' and hook 'working' yield a spinner in the ROW's own color (None). The prototype's Indicator model collapses these; preserve the distinction by mapping indeterminate/working to ProgressState::Plain and normal/paused/error to their colored states even when pct is None.
pct==0 must render '0%', not be dropped as falsy. Python guards with `is not None` and isdigit(); Option<u8>==Some(0) must survive.
INACTIVE_STATES is exactly {"", "hidden"} and 'empty title/empty state never matches' semantics: empty pb_state (old tmux) and 'hidden' both mean no OSC indicator; do not extend or shrink this set.

Row text formatting asymmetry: pane rows are format!("   {branch}{active}{index}: {title}") with NO space after branch and a glued single-char active marker; agent rows are format!("   {branch} {label}") WITH a space and no active marker. Easy to unify by accident and drift 1 column.
Header rows carry a single leading space (" WINDOWS", " <AGENT>") — trimming breaks alignment.

Two distinct selection keys for the same window (RowKey::Window vs RowKey::AgentWindow(agent,id)) must remain distinct, and the agent-row key must include the pane (a session can be filed under multiple windows). Collapsing keys breaks nav/activate uniqueness assumed by the client.

Agent section ordering is sorted(set(agent names)) — dedup THEN Unicode-order sort. Iterate windows in fetch_windows (tmux list-windows) order in both the top section and each agent section; group membership order follows the sessions slice.

fit counts CODE POINTS, not display columns (Python len()). The right-edge indicator reserve math in the painter (reserve = indicator_char_count + 1; draw only when field >= reserve + 1) is built on the same char-count assumption. Introducing unicode-width in one place and not the other desyncs truncation.
Window-with-zero-panes emits just its heading (Python last = len-1 = -1, loop body never runs); empty group sections are skipped via the is_empty guard — replicate both guards exactly.

'animating' detection: Python derives it by testing whether any built row's indicator string is in the spinner-glyph set. The Rust client must derive it from Indicator::indeterminate() over the semantic rows instead of a glyph-membership test, or an Attention '●' / a percentage could be misclassified.
pane_progress default: pane not present must default to ("", None) (inactive), never panic on a missing key.
Legacy/empty color name "" for an agent session must fall back to the default agent color at paint time (Python pair 2 / prototype Color::Cyan), not be treated as an error.
